hero.title: Tools for the camera department.
hero.lede: Four free apps, built by a cinematographer for the needs of the set. One keeps your footage safe, one sends it, one checks it on arrival, one brings it back.
b.role: Offload camera cards, verify every copy.
b.myth: Bandua offloads camera cards to several drives at once, checks every copy against the source with a hash, and writes a log, an MHL and a PDF report for the editor or the lab. Bandua is a protective deity of the western Iberian Peninsula. Here, it watches over your footage.
b.feat:
• Copies in a single pass to one, two or more destinations at the same time.
  • Verifies every copy on the drive itself: each copy is read back with the system cache bypassed and compared by hash (xxHash64 by default, XXH3, MD5 or SHA-1). A file only gets its final name once it is verified.
  • Reads the card a second time (on by default) to catch a faulty card reader, cable or card.
  • Watches the card during the offload: a file that changes, appears or disappears fails the offload, so you never format a card that was still being written to.
  • Copies the card exactly as it is: RED, ARRI, Blackmagic, Sony, Canon, GoPro, DJI, without system junk files. RED .RDC folders are listed as one clip each.
  • Writes 4 reports in each dated folder: PDF, text log, MHL (readable by Silverstack, ShotPut, Hedge) and JSON.
  • Re-verifies an existing folder from its MHL, before you format a card or deliver a drive, with progress, a status for each clip (verified, damaged, missing) and its own PDF report.
  • Checks free space before starting, and keeps destinations and project info so you can chain cards.
b.steps:
• Click Source and select the card.
  • Add one or more destinations.
  • Fill in the project, shoot day, camera and card. The card number comes from the clip names.
  • Click Start offload.
  • Wait for CARD VERIFIED before you format the card.
b.folder: Each destination gets a dated folder, such as 2026-11-06_1633_PROJECT_D03_A_A003.
dl.title: Download Bandua
b.dl: Ready to run. No Rust, no command line. The app is not signed yet, so your system warns you once on first launch: on Windows click “More info” then “Run anyway”, on macOS double-click the app, then open System Settings > Privacy & Security and click “Open Anyway”.
b.warn: Bandua helps you copy and verify media but does not replace your own checks. Never format a card before checking that every copy is complete and readable.
l.role: Send footage straight to the other computer, verified on arrival.
l.myth: Lugus Transfer sends footage from one computer to another with a link and a code. No server to run, no cloud storage, no account: the files go directly from one machine to the other, encrypted end to end. Every file is read back from the recipient's disk and compared with the source, and an MHL is written on arrival. Lugus is the messenger god of the Celtiberians, god of roads and exchanges. Noctiluca, the moon goddess of the Tartessian coast, lights the way and watches over overnight transfers.
l.feat:
• Direct transfer from one computer to the other, Mac or PC, with nothing stored anywhere else. Both computers just need to be on at the same time.
  • A link and a short code, to send through two different channels. The code never travels on the network: 3 attempts per code, and someone who only has the link can do nothing with it.
  • Choose what you send, choose what you receive: folders or files, from one or several drives, added one after another, then originals, proxies, sidecar files or file by file. Proxies arrive first.
  • Verified on the recipient's disk: each file is read back with the system cache bypassed and compared, block by block and as a whole, with the hash of the source. A file only gets its final name once it is verified.
  • Resumes exactly where it stopped after a network cut, a closed window or a computer gone to sleep, with the same progress on both screens.
  • MHL on arrival (MHL 1.1, xxHash64), readable by Bandua MHL Companion, Silverstack, ShotPut Pro, Hedge… and a delivery receipt for the sender.
  • Noctiluca mode: schedule the reception for the night, then put the computer to sleep or shut it down once everything is verified.
l.steps:
• Drop a folder or files on the window and untick what should not go.
  • Click Create the link and send the link and the code to the recipient.
  • On the other computer, paste the link, type the code and choose the destination.
  • Choose the files to receive, then click Receive the selection.
  • Wait for RECEIVED AND VERIFIED. The MHL is in the received folder.
l.how: The sender publishes its address in the BitTorrent DHT, then the two computers connect directly over QUIC, or through an encrypted relay when no direct route exists. The files never go anywhere else.
l.dl: Install it on both computers. The app is not signed yet, so your system warns you once on first launch: on Windows click “More info” then “Run anyway”, on macOS double-click the app, then open System Settings > Privacy & Security and click “Open Anyway”. If your system asks whether Lugus Transfer may use the network, allow it.
l.warn: Lugus Transfer helps you transfer and verify media but does not replace your own checks. Never delete the original before checking that the received copy is complete and readable.
c.role: Received the footage? Check that nothing broke on the way.
c.myth: Bandua MHL Companion is for the people who receive the footage: editor, assistant editor, lab, post-production, director. Drop the folder, start the check, and it reads every file back, compares it to the MHL that came with it, and tells you clip by clip what is intact and what is corrupt, missing or incomplete. It is the companion of Bandua: Bandua writes the MHL on set, the Companion checks it at the other end. It also reads the MHL files written by Silverstack, ShotPut Pro, Hedge and others.
c.feat:
• Finds every MHL in the folder you drop: several shoot days, cameras and cards at once, or a single .mhl file.
  • Reads MHL 1.1 and ASC MHL: Bandua, Silverstack, ShotPut Pro, Hedge, YoYotta… ASC MHL histories are merged across generations, and a history modified after the fact is flagged.
  • Reads every file back from the drive with the system cache bypassed, and compares its hash (xxHash64, XXH3, XXH128, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, C4…).
  • Names the problem clips: corrupt, missing, incomplete or unreadable, with the clip name (RED .RDC folders, ARRI, BRAW…) and a button to show the file.
  • Lists the files no MHL covers, so you know what could not be checked.
  • Exports a text report to send back to the production or the DIT. A command line tool is included for scripts.
  • Read only: nothing is ever changed or added next to the footage.
c.steps:
• Drop the footage folder onto the window, or choose it.
  • Check the list of MHL files found.
  • Click Start the check.
  • Wait for FOOTAGE INTACT, or open the Problems tab to see which clips to ask for again.
  • Export the report if you need to send it.
c.trust: A check only means something if the MHL comes from the person who made the original copy, ideally sent separately from the footage.
c.warn: Bandua MHL Companion helps you check media but does not replace your own checks and backups. Keep the original drive until the check is done.
a.role: Recover lost footage, repair broken clips.
a.myth: Ataecina reads camera cards, finds deleted files and files from a card formatted by mistake, restores a damaged card format, and repairs broken MOV and MP4 clips with a healthy reference clip. Ataecina is a goddess of the ancient Iberian Peninsula, often read as “the Reborn”. Like her, it brings back to light images we thought were lost.
a.featr:
• Card reading (exFAT, FAT32): original names and folders, deleted files, deep search after a format, boot sector restored from its backup copy.
  • PhotoRec search for every card format: MOV, MP4, BRAW, R3D, ARRIRAW, MXF, even files in pieces.
  • Card image first, the GNU ddrescue way: healthy areas first, damaged areas last, resume after an interruption.
a.featp:
• Batch repair with untrunc and one or more reference clips, normal mode then step mode.
  • Checks with ffprobe, and a full decode with ffmpeg if you ask. Thumbnails and a journal.csv.
  • Original files are never modified.
a.tools: Ataecina drives free tools you install from their official sites: untrunc, FFmpeg and TestDisk / PhotoRec.
a.dl: For Windows. The app is not signed yet: Windows warns you once, click “More info” then “Run anyway”. Reading a card directly needs administrator rights, and Ataecina offers to restart itself as administrator when needed.
a.where: Put untrunc, FFmpeg and PhotoRec next to Ataecina.exe, in a tools folder, or in your PATH. You can also set their location in the app.
sg.title: Security warnings when you download or open the apps
sg.p1: My apps (Bandua, Bandua MHL Companion, Ataecina and Lugus Transfer) are not signed, so your browser, Windows and macOS show a warning when you download or open them. They are not infected and contain no malicious code: the source code is public on my GitHub.
sg.p2: They are only downloadable from my GitHub repositories (github.com/tetsujin28). If a copy shows up anywhere else, it is not mine and it may be dangerous.
sg.win: Windows: in the “Windows protected your PC” window, click “More info”, then “Run anyway”.
sg.mac: macOS: double-click the app, then close the blocking message (do not move the app to the Trash). Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down to the Security section, click “Open Anyway” next to the app's name, then confirm with your session password. This is only asked once.
sg.mac2: If the button does not appear, open Terminal and type the following command (drag the app onto the window after the space), then press Enter: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine
ab.p1: I work behind the camera on fiction films and commercial productions. Born in Barcelona, I live and work in France, and I shoot mostly on Blackmagic, RED and ARRI cameras.
ab.p2: I also write code. Bandua, Lugus Transfer, Bandua MHL Companion and Ataecina started as tools I needed on my own shoots: one to offload cards without a doubt in mind, one to send the footage to the editor without a server in between, one so the editor can check the footage that reaches them, one for the day a card goes wrong. They are free because every camera department, and everyone after it, should have them.
ab.p3: Found a bug, or have an idea? Open an issue on the project page. Feedback from the set is what makes them better.
